title: What is known about 1RB---_1LC0RF_1RF0LD_0LE1LC_0RC0LC_1RB0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1LC0RF_1RF0LD_0LE1LC_0RC0LC_1RB0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. The head sweeps over the whole tape, which is almost all 1010… broken into domains by small defects that keep changing. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the halting configurations and no halt in the first 107 steps. The domain structure below is observed in simulations, not proved. No halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: B with 1 under the head, 1 right, 1 two right; C with 0 under the head, 1 right, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 42,805 cells have been visited and 21,447 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).

claims.title: F never reads 1 with a 1 to its right (so far)
claims.text: The only halting entry is A reading a 1, and A is entered only from F>1 (write 0, move right): the machine halts exactly when F>1 1 occurs. In the first 108 steps A is entered 267,524 times, always onto a 0; the window around the head is 110[0]101 or 100[0]101 in 261,362 of them.

claims.title: Domains of 10 and 01 with moving defects
claims.text: The tape is a period-2 background (density of 1s 0.501 at 109 steps) cut into domains (10)^k and (01)^k by defects 000, 0000, a single 1 or 0. Domain lengths range from 3 to about 100, and from one left-end visit to the next many of them change: the defects move, merge and split.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 16, history 1 up to width 14, history 2 up to width 13, history 3 up to width 12, LRU history up to width 2 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 12, p = 3 up to width 12, p = 4 up to width 12, p = 6 up to width 12. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..9; n = 10 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No regular macro structure has been found: the defects behave like interacting particles on a periodic background. A proof would need either a finite description of the defect dynamics (which defect pairs can meet and what they produce) or an invariant language for the whole tape; the halting pattern F>1 1 needs two adjacent 1s, which the background 1010… never has, so it can only come from a defect.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine fills its tape with 1010…, broken into stretches by little defects (three or four 0s in a row, or a lone extra 1). The head sweeps back and forth and every sweep moves the defects around, with no pattern found so far.

facts.text: No halt, checked by Lean's kernel (10<sup>7</sup> by compiled code).
No halt in the C simulator.
Entries into the halting state A in 10<sup>8</sup> steps, all onto a 0.

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The only halting entry is A reading a 1. A is entered only from F reading a 1 (F writes 0 and moves right), so the machine halts exactly when F>1 1 occurs: F on a 1 with another 1 right of it. In the first 108 steps that moment is reached 267,524 times and the next cell has always been a 0, nearly always as in 110[0]101 (157,870 times) or 100[0]101 (103,492 times), where [0] is the cell A lands on.
The background 1010… never has two adjacent 1s, so a halt could only happen at a defect.

sections.heading: Domains and defects
html: When the head reaches a new cell at the left end, the start of the tape looks like

Every stretch is the same background 1010…; (10)^k and (01)^k just say which phase it is in. The defects that separate them, 000, 0000, a lone 1 (two 1s in a row), change between visits; the right side looks the same. No block of the tape stays fixed for long and no counter is visible, so the run has not been reduced to rules.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).
After 109 steps the tape spans 42,805 cells (16,131 left of the start, 15,207 right), with a density of 1s of 0.501.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer over a tape of 10/01 domains separated by small defects (000, 0000, a lone 1); the domains and defects change irregularly from sweep to sweep, with no stable block structure in 10^8 steps. No regime proved.
family: bouncer over an irregular 10/01 domain gas
